title: Branded 404 page
description:
Replaced Next.js's stock white 404 — jarring on a site that commits to a dark ground — with a Night Field page: mono 404 eyebrow in accent ink, the statement in Futura at section-head scale, and an accent-underlined way back. Copy lives in content/site.json as a notFound block so it is a content diff, not a code diff. It returns HTTP 404 rather than redirecting home: the user asked whether 404s could bounce to the main site, and the answer given was no — that is a soft 404, which moves a visitor without telling them the link was wrong and reports a dead URL to crawlers as a live one. A branded page that still answers 404 keeps the honest status and the visitor's bearings. The user then tightened the copy from 'That page doesn't exist' plus an explanatory second sentence down to just 'This page doesn't exist.', which is the more restrained reading the design system asks for.

SCOPE VERDICT. All five project deliverables were already resolved before this cycle and none changed status here; this is polish inside the delivered rebuild and adds no deliverable. Three delivered earlier (rebuild, redesign, design exploration). One delivered in this session's preceding assist cycle: nseldeib.com now serves the rebuilt site, apex and www moved onto the nadia-website Vercel project with Namecheap DNS repointed. One still DEFERRED: publish live at nadiaeldeib.com — it remains on GitHub Pages, and the cutover is deliberately still owed. The ordering trap for whoever does it is recorded in .codeyam/SESSION-HANDOFF.md: merging rebuild-nextjs into main triggers a Pages rebuild, and Pages cannot build a Next.js app, so DNS must move off Pages first and the root CNAME must survive until Pages is disabled.

Zero extractions and zero new tests, both deliberate. app/not-found.tsx is already composition-only, and NotFound is a single visual block — splitting three sibling elements into three components would be structure for its own sake. Reuse of SectionHead was considered and rejected: it renders a number/label pair and the 404 eyebrow is a single token. No unit test because this project has NO component-testing infrastructure at all — no @testing-library, no jsdom, no browser environment in vitest.config.ts — and all twenty-plus existing components are covered by scenarios, not tests. Writing one would have meant adding dependencies and rewiring the runner for a three-element static page.

NotFoundPage is recorded as a trivial-wrapper rather than scenario-covered, and the reason matters beyond this feature: an application scenario at the real route is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE here. The capture pipeline treats HTTP 404 as a failed capture — it settled, restarted the dev server, retried, then refused, persisting a screenshot-less ghost scenario that had to be deleted with `editor delete`. Since 404 is this page's correct response, no application scenario can ever exist for it. Visual coverage comes from the component scenario notfound-default; the taxonomy checklist for the view is complete with all eight archetypes statused.

One environmental fix worth carrying forward, and it probably explains the previous cycle's unresolved note. `.codeyam/editor.json` sets proxy.controlPort=14350, but this editor serves the __codeyam_preview prefix on its real control port 59910 (container.log: 'Container ready controlPort=59910 proxyHttpPort=14251 appPort=3000'). Nothing was ever going to bind 14350; the stale value reached the capture through get-preview-state source=disk-fallback, and every preview and capture failed ECONNREFUSED. Overriding proxy.controlPort to 59910 in the gitignored .codeyam/editor.local.json fixed capture outright. The previous cycle recorded 'the codeyam preview cannot reach the database, nothing listens on 14252' as an unexplained limitation — same subsystem, very likely the same class of stale-port config. A demo-skip was recorded before the fix was found and then re-recorded correcting itself, because the original claimed a structural proxy failure that was not true.

Not verified, stated as such: the mobile viewport. A browser window resize did not change the captured viewport, so the 860px media query rests only on being a direct copy of Footer.module.css's existing rule rather than on a look. Everything else is measured — tsc passes, all 35 isolation routes return 200, recapture-stale restored 15 frames pixel-identical with zero visual diffs, scenario-review reports 0 duplicates and 0 stale across 36 targets, and the audit passed with 68 glossary entries covered.
